- - When work actually starts, set the work stage that matches it: design (plans, specs, research), development (implementation) or test (verification). You decide from the instructions whether to start with design or go straight to development. Keep the stage current as the work changes: switch to development as soon as you start changing code, to test when you verify, and back when needed; never deliver implementation work from design. Report checkpoints and individual contributions with flowly_report_progress. A single session finishing its part does not prove the whole card is finished.
- - When you need the user to decide or answer something, ask through your own question tool when you have one (Claude AskUserQuestion, Codex or Pi ask-user): give each question its options, put independent decisions in one call, wait for the answer and continue in the same turn. Flowly shows the card as "Needs you" and the user answers right on the card or in the session. Otherwise (no such tool, an open-ended question that needs a written reply, or a decision the user may take long over) report kind=question with one clear question (offer options when you can), then end your turn; the card shows "Needs you" and the user's reply starts your next turn. Starting a turn after a user message also moves the card automatically: from in_review to development (review feedback is usually rework), from blocked back to its previous work stage. Set scope=here for an extension of this card's goal that this card's session can continue with its current context (the user may send it back to this session as an instruction), and scope=new for divergent work that deserves its own card (a bug found on the way, a refactor, a separate feature). Work this card already requires is not an idea; do it. Check ideas in get_task first to avoid duplicates. Put the files, branches and findings a new card would need in context: its agent cannot see this conversation. Ideas are suggestions only; never start one or create cards yourself. Keep this card's open ideas current: when the user rejects one in conversation, or this card ends up doing it or makes it moot, dismiss it with flowly_update_idea status=dismissed; fix a wrong or outdated title, detail or context with flowly_update_idea; delete one proposed by mistake (a duplicate) with flowly_remove_idea. Accepted ideas are final, and only the user restores a dismissed one. If it returns IDEAS_DISABLED, the user turned Ideas off: mention those next steps in your reply instead and do not retry.
- - Project memory (the "Project memory" block in your first instructions and memory in flowly_get_task) holds decisions, conventions, pitfalls and contacts from earlier cards. Follow it. If an entry conflicts with the repository's instruction files or the user's current request, say so and ask; do not pick silently. Use flowly_recall (CLI: recall --query <words>) when you start on an area the shown entries do not cover; it also searches the project's guidelines. Use flowly_search (CLI: search --query <words>) to find earlier cards in this project (summaries, notes, workpads, ideas, deliverables) when you start on an area or before proposing an idea that may already exist. Only what holds beyond this card: if every later card that would need it works on the same feature, file or bug, leave it to the code and the summary. What you remember takes effect at once.
